solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Grumbler — mean or crazy? (6)

indicatorNotes.crazy: Crazy letters are out of their right order.

blocks.note: the six letters of MEAN OR rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone sizing up a moaner and wondering whether they are nasty or just unhinged.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words 'mean or' look like part of the question but are the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A moaner is someone who grumbles.

entries.clue: Fashionable instant meal (6)

blocks.note: a mo is a moment
a dish is a meal or course

annotation.surface: A trendy ready meal, the kind you microwave in a minute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Instant meal' reads as one thing, but 'instant' is a noun here: a mo, as in 'wait a mo'.
annotation.definitionFit: Modish means in the current fashion.

entries.clue: Paying heed at tense conclusion (9)

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
an ending is a conclusion

annotation.surface: Someone listening closely as a nail-biting story reaches its climax.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the conclusion; it is the grammatical tense, abbreviated T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to attend is to listen or give heed, as in 'attend to what I say'.

entries.clue: English literature, fifth of subjects chosen (5)

annotation.definitionNote: ELITE is a noun and 'chosen' an adjective, but 'the chosen' and 'the elite' swap freely.

indicatorNotes.fifth of: Fifth of a word is its fifth letter.

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
lit is short for literature
the fifth letter of S-U-B-J-E-C-T-S

annotation.surface: A school timetable listing English literature as one of the subjects a pupil has chosen.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a list of exam options; only the last word is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The elite are the chosen few, the select best of a group.

entries.clue: Improvement in Hampshire for many (6)

indicatorNotes.in: The answer sits in the letters of the words that follow.

blocks.note: hampshiRE FOR Many

annotation.surface: A local change in Hampshire that benefits many residents.
annotation.walkthrough: Hampshire is an English county, which makes it sound like a real place is under discussion; it just houses the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a reform is a change made to put something right.

entries.clue: Guards heading off for gates? (7)

indicatorNotes.heading off: Taking off the head drops the first letter.

blocks.note: guards are SENTRIES; heading off drops the first letter S

annotation.surface: Sentries stepping away to stand watch at the gates.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'gates' as a loose definition: entries are ways in, as gates are.
annotation.definitionFit: Entries are entrances, and gates are ways of entry.

entries.clue: Member of Parliament depressed, first to last (3)

indicatorNotes.first to last: Move the first letter to the end.

blocks.note: depressed is LOW; its first letter L moves to the end

annotation.surface: A gloomy MP sinking to the bottom of the pecking order.
annotation.walkthrough: A group of owls is called a parliament, so an owl is a member of one; the capital P hides this.
annotation.definitionFit: A parliament is the collective noun for owls.

entries.clue: Month on edge — an unsettling experience (6)

indicatorNotes.on: In a down clue, 'on' places the first piece on top of the next.

blocks.note: May is a month
a hem is the edge of cloth

annotation.surface: A month spent on edge, full of nerves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as a single phrase meaning nervous; split it, and 'on' only says the month comes first in a down answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or chaos, which leaves everyone involved shaken.

entries.clue: Terribly tired in the mind, to ill effect (13)

blocks.note: TIRED rearranged
mentally means in the mind

annotation.surface: Someone so exhausted that their thinking suffers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terribly tired' reads as 'very tired'; 'terribly' is the signal to rearrange TIRED.
annotation.definitionFit: Detrimentally means in a harmful way, to ill effect.

entries.clue: Excluding physical exercise, surprisingly I tend to be fit (9)

indicatorNotes.surprisingly: Letters arranged surprisingly are in an unexpected order.

blocks.note: ex means without, as in ex-dividend
PE is physical education, school exercise
I TEND rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone who skips the gym yet still manages to stay in shape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fit' suggests physical fitness; here it means suitable, the sense of expedient.
annotation.definitionFit: Expedient means suitable or fitting for the purpose.

entries.clue: One getting left out to suffer superficial damage? (5)

indicatorNotes.getting left out: Left is L, and it is taken out.

blocks.note: one is SINGLE; L for left is taken out

annotation.surface: Someone excluded from the group ends up quietly hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left out' sounds like social exclusion; it is the letter L being removed.
annotation.definitionFit: To singe is to burn slightly, damage only on the surface.

entries.clue: Run into difficulty and feel a stinging sensation (7)

indicatorNotes.into: The first piece goes into the second.

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
in a pickle means in difficulty

annotation.surface: Someone who hits trouble and feels the sting of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run into difficulty' reads as one phrase; split it, R goes inside PICKLE.
annotation.definitionFit: To prickle is the tingling feeling of skin touched by nettles or pins.

entries.clue: Depression in front of a computer screen? (9)

annotation.definition: Depression in front of a computer screen?

blocks.note: the surface pushes low mood; the setter means a pressing down, as of a key

blocks.clueFragment: in front of a computer screen?
blocks.note: where the keyboard sits, so the thing pressed is a key

annotation.surface: A person sitting glumly at their computer, feeling down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' is the physical pressing down of a key, not low mood.
annotation.definitionFit: A keystroke is a key pressed down on the keyboard in front of the screen.

entries.clue: Shamelessness of my demo: it’s out of order (9)

indicatorNotes.out of order: Letters out of order are rearranged.

blocks.note: MY DEMO ITS rearranged

annotation.surface: A performer admitting their demo tape was brazenly inappropriate.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is split across the colon; the apostrophe in 'it's' is dropped.
annotation.definitionFit: Immodesty is a lack of shame or modesty.

entries.clue: Gas satisfied hotel — a new source of energy (7)

blocks.note: a need met is a need satisfied
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
E is the physics symbol for energy; 'source of' is surface padding

annotation.surface: A hotel pleased with its new gas supply as an energy source.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Source of energy' looks like a gloss on the gas, but it just supplies E.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: methane is one gas among many, the main part of natural gas.

entries.clue: A Liberal was deceitful in league with others (6)

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
lied means was deceitful

annotation.surface: A politician caught lying while in a coalition with other parties.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a political scandal; the definition is only the last four words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: nations allied by treaty are in league with each other.

entries.clue: Group of workers sealing terms ultimately for agreement (6)

indicatorNotes.sealing: The outer piece seals the other inside it.
indicatorNotes.ultimately: Ultimately points to the last letter.

blocks.note: a trade union is a group of workers
the last letter of terms

annotation.surface: A trade union finally signing off a deal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface talks of sealing terms as in closing a deal; 'sealing' puts S inside UNION.
annotation.definitionFit: Singers in unison sing one note together, so the word came to mean full accord.

entries.clue: Messenger last to see person receiving gift (7)

indicatorNotes.last to: Last to a word is its final letter.

blocks.note: a legate is an envoy, often papal
the final letter of see

annotation.surface: A courier who is the last to see the recipient of a delivery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last to see' reads as a messenger arriving late; it is the final letter of 'see'.
annotation.definitionFit: A legatee receives a legacy, a gift left in a will.

entries.clue: Hit it off and made progress (3,2)

blocks.note: to hit it off is to become friendly at once
to get on is to advance

annotation.surface: Two people who got along and moved forward together.
annotation.walkthrough: Got on means both got along with someone and advanced.
annotation.definitionFit: People who hit it off got on well; someone who made progress got on.

entries.clue: Spirits dope one repeatedly (5)

indicatorNotes.repeatedly: Repeatedly means the piece is used twice.

blocks.note: gen and dope are both slang for information
I is the Roman numeral for one
the I again

annotation.surface: Someone spiking a drink with spirits again and again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dope' here is information, not drugs; gen is British slang for the same thing.
annotation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genie, spirits of Arabian legend.

entries.clue: Immediate sensation aunt produced somehow (13)

indicatorNotes.produced somehow: Produced somehow means made in some other arrangement.

blocks.note: SENSATION AUNT rearranged

annotation.surface: An aunt causing an instant stir.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Immediate sensation' looks like one noun phrase; only 'Immediate' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something instantaneous happens at once, with no delay.

entries.clue: The total amount? Just a bit of it, by the sound of it (3)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: What is said, not what is written.

blocks.note: some means a bit of it

annotation.surface: Someone asking for the whole amount and getting only a portion.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that the whole and a part are pronounced the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A sum is the figure reached when everything is added up.

entries.clue: Young woman belonging to Amsterdam’s elite (6)

indicatorNotes.belonging to: The answer belongs to, sits within, the words that follow.

blocks.note: amsterDAM'S ELite

annotation.surface: A young woman from Amsterdam high society.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored when reading the run of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old, storybook word for a young unmarried woman, as in 'damsel in distress'.

entries.clue: Bird, one flying by animal on farm (6)

indicatorNotes.flying: Flying letters scatter into a new order.
indicatorNotes.by: 'By' in its sense of beside, so the farm animal stands right next to the rearranged ONE.

blocks.note: a pig is a farm animal
ONE rearranged

annotation.surface: A bird flying past a farmyard animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One flying' seems to describe the bird; it tells you to rearrange ONE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the pigeon is a common bird, seen in every city square.
